messages:
maria g.: Heads-up — seeing a race where clients get X-Backpressure-Delay + 429 and SDKs retry immediately instead of honoring delay; doubles inflight and skews quota/dashboard numbers.
kevin: Can you paste a minimal repro or logs?
maria g.: logs: 
```
2024-04-11T02:14:10Z router -> client 429 X-Backpressure-Delay: 500
client SDK retries at t+0 -> router accepts -> duplicate inflight
```
priya: That matches the router change we pushed yesterday: overcommit path now returns 429 with a delay header (we switched from 503 to 429 to preserve client-level retry semantics). Didn't realize SDKs would ignore the delay header.
sam: By default our SDKs treat 429 as immediate retryable. We need to add explicit parsing for the header and schedule retry after the delay instead of instant retry.
priya: Minimal API we want: response.headers['X-Backpressure-Delay'] (ms) and response.headers['X-Quota-Bucket'] for attribution. SDK surface: response.backpressure_delay_ms?: number, response.quota_bucket?: string.
kevin: Agree. We should standardize field names across Py/TS/Go. Also add a callback/hook so apps can opt-out of automatic delayed retry.
maria g.: Concern: changing default retry timing is technically breaking for apps that relied on immediate retry. Suggest opt-in flag 'honor_backpressure_headers' default false for initial rollout.
sam: I can do python change + docs. Propose: default=false, and Console can flip per-org flag for canary customers.
kevin: I'll implement TS + Go. Will expose: clientConfig.honorBackpressureHeaders: boolean and a response.meta.backpressureDelayMs.
console-signal: For dashboarding we need new metrics: backpressure_events count, avg_delay_ms, and mapping to quota buckets so we can show which customers/routes hit backpressure.
priya: Router will start emitting X-Quota-Bucket with stable IDs; I'll add that header in the next router patch. Need SDKs to capture it and surface it for telemetry.
maria g.: Rollout plan outline: 1) Stabilize router header (X-Backpressure-Delay, X-Quota-Bucket). 2) Land SDK changes behind flag (py/ts/go). 3) Release canary SDKs (tags) + enable flag for 10% orgs via Console. 4) Add console tile and traces to show backpressure events. 5) Monitor for regressions 24-48h and then broaden.
kevin: Tests: unit parse header, integration test simulating header + ensure client waits, and e2e with router in staging. Quick curl to simulate: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "X-Backpressure-Delay: 500" -d '{"input":"test"}'
```
sam: I'll add migration notes to CHANGELOG and a short 'what changed' in SDK docs. Also mention that apps using custom retry logic might need to adjust.
priya: One more infra thing — ensure proxies don't strip the header (edge/proxy teams, FYI).
maria g.: Concrete owners: Kevin -> TS/Go PRs + tests; Sam -> Python PR + docs; Priya -> router header + rollout flag; Maria -> coordination, console tile backlog and rollout comms.
kevin: I'll start PRs today, ETA 2 business days for initial PRs.
sam: ETA 2 days for python + docs.
console-signal: Created console task to add KPI tiles and will link PRs.
maria g.: deploy-bot: schedule canary window? :calendar:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy window reserved for 2024-04-12 03:00 UTC. Watch #incidents if error-rate spikes.
kevin: If we see >2x baseline error rate or duplicate-inflight increase revert the flag immediately.
maria g.: Thanks — will follow up with a short migration note and the per-org opt-in instructions.
